metric.why: Idle servers burn power, licenses, and depreciation while producing nothing. Fleet utilization is where the money hides in most enterprise estates, and it is the denominator that makes every efficiency metric honest.
metric.definition: The share of provisioned compute doing real work, measured over time rather than at peak.

reading.body:
Server utilization rate is the metric that reveals whether provisioned compute is earning its keep, because idle servers consume power, licenses, and depreciation at nearly the same rate as busy ones.

A low utilization rate means a data center is paying the full cost of capacity while delivering a fraction of the output. For AI workloads, this matters acutely: GPU clusters carry high capital cost and high idle power draw, so underutilization is not a rounding error but a structural drain on the economics of scaling. The denominator problem is real, as efficiency ratios built on peak demand rather than sustained throughput will consistently flatter the actual picture.

The data here covers the definition and rationale for tracking this metric, not its measured values across any fleet or facility. It does not report what typical or target utilization rates look like, nor how AI-specific infrastructure compares to general enterprise estates. Readers wanting benchmark figures or trend data will need to look beyond what this entry provides.
